pages.head: Welcome
pages.html:
Welcome

Show the Count is a Starter: a small game that shows a few Game-Maker ideas, with signs in the levels that say what you are looking at. It has two short levels and takes a couple of minutes to finish.

Play it first. Then open it in Game-Maker (Edit a copy on the home page keeps the original safe) and read the pages below, which say where each thing in the levels is made.

The keys

Left and Right walk. Space jumps. Up and Down climb a ladder. F2 shows your lives, hit points and score. Walk into the door at the end of a level to go on.

A dark bulb adds one to a counter you carry, and lights up. The lit bulbs show the count, because the game has no way to print it as a number. Nothing in this game hurts you.

pages.head: Level 1: Light the Meter
pages.html:
Level 1: Light the Meter

The LIT BULBS SHOW YOUR COUNT sign stands at the start. A ladder leads up to a ledge, and along the ledge is a row of five dark bulbs. A brick wall with a small blue gate in it stands further on, with the THIS GATE TAKES FIVE sign in front of it.

Walk into the gate first, if you like. It does not open: nothing is lit yet. Then climb up and walk along the ledge. Each bulb lights as you touch it and stays lit, so the row fills from left to right. Come back down and walk into the gate: with all five lit it opens and takes the count.

There are four coins on the ground, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 1 is made

  • The dark bulb. Open meter.bbl in the blocks editor and pick the dark bulb. It is not solid, so Lena walks through it. Its Changes counter is Special counter 3 by 1, and Becomes is the lit bulb, another block, so the bulb changes its picture instead of vanishing. Special counters are numbers 20 to 29 in the engine, free for a game to use.
  • The lit bulb. Pick it too. It does nothing at all. It is only a picture, and it is the whole meter: a row of lit and dark bulbs is the count, shown in the only way the game can show it.
  • The gate. Pick the five-slot gate. It is solid on all four sides. Its Changes counter is Special counter 3 by -5, and Becomes is the sky. A touch is refused if the counter cannot pay, so with four lit the gate does nothing.
  • The start. Open hero.chr in the Character Maker. The counter's Starts at is 1: the counter always holds one more than it shows, so 1 means nothing carried.
  • The signs. Each is a group of blocks in the map. They do nothing but talk.

pages.head: Level 2: The Full Meter
pages.html:
Level 2: The Full Meter

The SIX BULBS. FILL THE METER sign stands at the start. Three dark bulbs sit on the ground ahead, and three more along a ledge up the ladder. At the far end of the room the FULL METER OPENS EXIT sign stands by a brick wall with a gate with six slots in it.

There is no door in this room. Light all six bulbs and walk into the gate: it opens, takes the count and you walk straight on into the ending. With five lit it stays shut.

There are six coins along the ground, worth ten points each.

pages.head: How this level is made
pages.html:
How level 2 is made

  • The gate takes six. Pick the six-slot gate in meter.bbl. It is the same as the first level's gate, with Changes counter of Special counter 3 by -6 because this map holds exactly six bulbs. A gate that took seven could never open, and the Level check's Counters that run out would say so.
  • The gate is the door. Open meter.gam in the game editor. The level's only link starts on the gate's own block. A gate is solid until it is paid, then it becomes sky, and the next step into that block is the link to the next scene.
  • A fresh count. Counters travel from level to level, but level 1 spent all five, so this level starts at zero.
  • A longer meter. It is the same two blocks, used six times. A meter of ten needs ten bulbs in the map and a gate that takes ten. The game does not draw a meter for you: every step you want to see is a block you put there.

pages.head: What Game-Maker cannot do
pages.html:
What Game-Maker cannot do

Showing a count is a trick, and it has limits:

  • It cannot print a number. There is no block that shows what a counter holds. The status line shows hit points, lives and score, and F2 shows a few more, but not a special counter.
  • Each value needs its own picture. A meter of five steps is five bulbs, and a meter of fifty is fifty. The game does not draw a bar that grows.
  • The bulbs do not read the counter. A bulb adds one and changes its own picture, and nothing keeps the two in step. Take a bulb away from the map and the gate still wants the same price.
  • A lit bulb stays lit even after a gate spends the count. A meter that should empty again needs blocks that change back.
  • A counter has a number, not a name. Special counter 3 is the same number in every block that uses it, so keep a list of what each counter means.

pages.head: Make it yours
pages.html:
Make it yours

  • Add a sixth bulb to level 1's row. The gate still takes five, so one is spare.
  • Change level 1's gate to take 3 in the blocks editor. The first three bulbs now open it.
  • Take one bulb out of level 2's map. The six-slot gate can never open, and the Level check says so.
  • Draw a different lit picture, such as a star, and the meter changes with it.
  • Start the counter at 2 in hero.chr. Level 1 now needs only four bulbs.

The home page's Starters tab has more small games like this one.
